additions.reason: The Rebbe explicitly states that each tzaddik in the generation 'עוֹשֶׂה בְּחִינַת מִשְׁכָּן' (makes/IS a bechina of the Mishkan/Tabernacle). This is direct bechina language equating the tzaddik's spiritual work with the Mishkan. The Mishkan is the vessel through which the children receive their pure breath of Torah — it is the tzaddik's output/identity as shepherd. The concept מִשְׁכָּן belongs in Package 1 alongside רועה and משה as an aspect of the tzaddik's essential function. Additionally, the text connects the Mishkan to the opening of the book of Vayikra (וַיִּקְרָא — which begins from the completion of the Mishkan's erection), deepening its role as the structural vessel of the generation.
additions.source_quote: כָּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד לְפִי בְּחִינָתוֹ, הוּא עוֹשֶׂה בְּחִינַת מִשְׁכָּן

additions.reason: The Rebbe equates the tzaddik who can gather the good points of all Israel with the שליח ציבור (prayer leader/cantor). The teaching states: 'זֶה הַצַּדִּיק שֶׁאוֹחֵז בְּמַדְרֵגָה זֹאת, הוּא יָכוֹל לִהְיוֹת חַזָּן וּשְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר'. The שליח ציבור IS the one who gathers all the good points and prays with them — this is his essential bechina nature. He is sent by the entire congregation (נִקְרָא שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר, he is CALLED the congregation's agent) because all good points are included in him. This is pure bechina language (X נקרא Y / X is called Y = X IS Y at its essential level). The שליח ציבור belongs in Package 1 as an expression of the tzaddik-shepherd-Moses archetype.
additions.source_quote: הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל לִפְנֵי הָעַמּוּד, הוּא נִקְרָא שְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר... צָרִיךְ שֶׁיְּקַבֵּץ כָּל נְקֻדָּה טוֹבָה שֶׁנִּמְצָא בְּכָל אֶחָד מֵהַמִּתְפַּלְּלִין

additions.reason: The Rebbe equates the חזן (cantor) with the one who knows 'הֵיכָן הַתִּינוֹקוֹת קוֹרְאִים' — where the children learn (i.e., which tzaddik/shepherd their pure breath comes from). The Mishnah (Shabbat 11) is quoted: 'הַחַזָּן רוֹאֶה הֵיכָן הַתִּינוֹקוֹת קוֹרְאִים' — the חזן SEES where the children read, meaning he knows the whole spiritual geography of the generation's tzaddikim and their disciples. The חזן IS the one who can make nigguns AND who IS the שליח ציבור. He is thus a bechina of the tzaddik-shepherd-Moses cluster (Package 1). The חזן and שליח ציבור are used interchangeably in the teaching, but both point to the essential quality of the tzaddik who gathers good points.
additions.source_quote: הַחַזָּן, דְּהַיְנוּ מִי שֶׁיָּכוֹל לַעֲשׂוֹת הַנִּגּוּנִים הַנַּ"ל, שֶׁהוּא יָכוֹל לִהְיוֹת חַזָּן וּשְׁלִיחַ צִבּוּר

additions.reason: The concept of the 'good point' (נְקֻדָּה טוֹבָה) is the absolute center of Torah #282 — mentioned more times than any other concept. The Rebbe repeatedly says one must find 'אֵיזֶה נְקֻדָּה טוֹבָה' in every person, even the worst sinner. The good point IS the 'עוד' (the 'still/yet') that remains. The text uses explicit bechina language: 'עַל יְדֵי בְּחִינַת הָעוֹד שֶׁלִּי' (via the bechina of my 'still') — establishing that 'עוד' and 'נְקֻדָּה טוֹבָה' are the same essential thing. The נְקֻדָּה טוֹבָה belongs in Package 3 (the 'עוד מעט' cluster) as its most concrete expression.
additions.source_quote: כִּי צָרִיךְ הָאָדָם לְחַפֵּשׂ וּלְבַקֵּשׁ לִמְצֹא בְּעַצְמוֹ אֵיזֶה מְעַט טוֹב... כִּי אֵין אֶפְשָׁר שֶׁלֹּא יִהְיֶה בְּאוֹתָהּ הַמִּצְוָה... אֵיזֶה נְקֻדָּה טוֹבָה

additions.reason: The בַּעַל דָּבָר (the Adversary/Satan) is explicitly named as the force that tries to induce depression and sadness when a person looks at their own sins. The Rebbe says: 'רוֹצֶה הַבַּעַל דָּבָר לְהַפִּילוֹ עַל יְדֵי זֶה בְּעַצְבוּת וּמָרָה שְׁחוֹרָה'. The בעל דבר is the evil counterpart to the tzaddik who encourages self-finding of good points — he is the force that induces כַּף חוֹבָה (the scale of guilt). He is the evil mirror of the shepherd/Moses figure (Package 1). No bechina edge exists for this node in Torah #282 dataset, but it is an explicit evil actor with identity language ('all the falls in one's mind... are only the acts of the בעל דבר'). Suggested as an addition to a new evil package.
additions.source_quote: הַנְּפִילָה שֶׁבְּדַעְתּוֹ, וְהָעַצְבוּת וְהַמָּרָה שְׁחוֹרָה שֶׁנּוֹפֵל עָלָיו עַל־יְדֵי־זֶה, הַכֹּל הוּא רַק מַעֲשֵׂי בַּעַל דָּבָר

additions.reason: עַצְבוּת (sadness/depression) is named as the evil force that prevents prayer and brings a person to despair. The Rebbe contrasts שִׂמְחָה (joy, the positive goal) with עַצְבוּת (depression, the evil counterpart) throughout the teaching. The source text says: 'צָרִיךְ הָאָדָם לִזָּהֵר מְאֹד לִהְיוֹת בְּשִׂמְחָה תָּמִיד, וּלְהַרְחִיק הָעַצְבוּת מְאֹד מְאֹד'. The text also states that the extraction of nigguns is a bechina of 'מְלַקֵּט הָרוּחַ טוֹבָה מִן הָרוּחַ נְכֵאָה עַצְבוּת רוּחַ' — making עַצְבוּת and רוּחַ נְכֵאָה into bechina-equivalent terms (the sad/depressed spirit = the evil domain from which the good spirit is extracted). This is an implicit bechina. עַצְבוּת is the evil mirror of שִׂמְחָה and נְקֻדָּה טוֹבָה.
additions.source_quote: וּלְהַרְחִיק הָעַצְבוּת מְאֹד מְאֹד... הָרוּחַ נְכֵאָה עַצְבוּת רוּחַ

additions.reason: מָרָה שְׁחוֹרָה (melancholy/black bile) is repeatedly mentioned as the dark force that causes people to despair and fall away from God. The Rebbe groups it with עַצְבוּת throughout the teaching. In line 19: 'רֹב בְּנֵי אָדָם שֶׁרְחוֹקִים מֵהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ, עִקַּר רִחוּקָם הוּא מֵחֲמַת מָרָה שְׁחוֹרָה וְעַצְבוּת'. מרה שחורה and עצבות are effectively treated as bechina-equivalent (the same evil reality) in this teaching — both are aspects of the רוּחַ נְכֵאָה (the depressed spirit). A bechina edge מרה שחורה ↔ עצבות is strongly implied by the text's use of them interchangeably.
additions.source_quote: עִקַּר רִחוּקָם הוּא מֵחֲמַת מָרָה שְׁחוֹרָה וְעַצְבוּת

additions.reason: שִׂמְחָה (joy) is the explicit goal of the practice of finding good points. The Rebbe says finding one's good points leads to 'לָבוֹא לִידֵי שִׂמְחָה'. But more precisely, the teaching frames שִׂמְחָה as the positive state that IS the same as being in the spiritual domain of melody — the nigguns ARE joy. The text says: 'יְחַיֶּה וִישַׂמֵּחַ אֶת נַפְשׁוֹ' and this is tied directly to the niggun/good spirit extraction (Package 2). שִׂמְחָה is the experiential name for the same reality that מנגן בכלי זמר describes from the musical angle — both are expressions of the רוּחַ טוֹבָה being liberated from the רוּחַ נְכֵאָה. Likely belongs in Package 2 as the inner face of what the niggun produces/is.
additions.source_quote: צָרִיךְ הָאָדָם לְחַפֵּשׂ וּלְבַקֵּשׁ לִמְצֹא בְּעַצְמוֹ אֵיזֶה מְעַט טוֹב, כְּדֵי לְהַחֲיוֹת אֶת עַצְמוֹ, וְלָבוֹא לִידֵי שִׂמְחָה

additions.reason: כַּף זְכוּת (the scale of merit) is what a person is moved to when the good point is found. The Rebbe says that finding the good point in a person moves them 'מִכַּף חוֹבָה לְכַף זְכוּת' (from the scale of guilt to the scale of merit). The כף זכות and the 'עוד מעט טוב' are the same essential reality: the small good that tips the balance. This is the conceptual space of Package 3 — the theological category of the 'remaining good point.'
additions.source_quote: עַל־יְדֵי שֶׁמּוֹצְאִין בּוֹ עוֹד מְעַט טוֹב, אֵיזֶה נְקֻדָּה טוֹבָה, וְדָנִין אוֹתוֹ לְכַף זְכוּת, עַל־יְדֵי־זֶה מוֹצִיאִין אוֹתוֹ בֶּאֱמֶת מִכַּף חוֹבָה לְכַף זְכוּת

additions.reason: תְּשׁוּבָה (repentance/return to God) appears as the ultimate destination of the practice: finding the good point enables a person to return to God. However, the text uses both eitza language (finding good points LEADS TO teshuvah) and bechina-adjacent language ('עַל־יְדֵי שֶׁמּוֹצֵא בּוֹ מְעַט טוֹב... וְיוּכַל לַהֲשִׁיבוֹ בִּתְשׁוּבָה'). The connection between the 'remaining good point' and teshuvah is primarily eitza in this Torah (finding the point produces teshuvah), not bechina (they are not the same essential nature). Flagged here for completeness — teshuvah is named 13+ times in the text but its connection to the core bechina cluster is through eitza rather than bechina identity. A bechina edge is not clearly warranted by the text's language.
additions.source_quote: וְיוּכַל לָשׁוּב בִּתְשׁוּבָה... וִיצַפֶּה לִישׁוּעָה עֲדַיִן, וְיוּכַל לְהִתְפַּלֵּל וּלְזַמֵּר וּלְהוֹדוֹת לַה'

analysis_notes.summary: Torah #282 is a teaching with a compact bechina subgraph (only 4 edges, 7 nodes, 3 components) but a rich source text full of conceptual content. All 7 dataset nodes are cleanly assigned to packages — no orphans. The main gap is the almost total absence of bechina edges for the teaching's most prominent concepts: (1) נְקֻדָּה טוֹבָה is the heart of the entire teaching and should have multiple bechina edges; (2) the evil cluster (בעל דבר, עצבות, מרה שחורה) is not represented at all in the bechina dataset, despite being named explicitly and repeatedly; (3) the tzaddik functions (שליח ציבור, חזן, משכן) are named with bechina language in the text but are not in the dataset; (4) שמחה is the positive pole of the niggun cluster and is missing. The dataset appears to have captured only a skeleton of the full bechina structure of this teaching.
analysis_notes.evil_mirror_assessment: Torah #282 has a clear evil counterpart structure: the positive teaching (finding good points → joy → melody → prayer) is mirrored by the negative (seeing only sins → בעל דבר induces → depression/מרה שחורה → inability to pray). The evil mirror package {בעל דבר, עצבות, מרה שחורה, כף חובה} is completely absent from the bechina dataset. This is a significant gap.
